# Vela-2.0-0.3B

The previous default decision model, a ModernBERT encoder for a CPU. It answers set and span questions as well, with calibrated thresholds for the built-in questions.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B), pinned at `a3209a50dc3e` |
| Family | [Vela 2.0](model-runtime/supported-models/vela-2/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 0.309B loaded |
| Backbone | ModernBERT |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | FP32 on every device |
| Weights | about 1.2 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 4 GiB or more |
| Reads | text |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | Yes |
| `set` | Yes |
| `span` | Yes, on the `router` span head |

## Built-in questions

The Vela 2.0 family was trained on the Router's built-in
questions, so the Router asks each one in its trained form; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) lists which.

A rule without a `predicate` takes this model's calibrated threshold:

| Preset | Threshold |
| --- | ---: |
| jailbreak (`jailbreak`) | 0.75 |
| domain (`domain`) | 0.28 |
| pii (`pii`) | 0.01 |
| fact check (`fact_check`) | 0.93 |
| user feedback (`feedback`) | 0.37 |
| safety (`harm`) | 0.46 |
| modality (`modality`) | 0.51 |

## Hardware

Each time it loads, the model compares its answers with the reference
answers recorded for its revision. They are recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu`)
- NVIDIA Hopper (sm_90) (`cuda:sm_90`)
- Ascend NPU (`npu`)
- AMD GPU (ROCm) (`rocm`)

Where a hardware reference and its device class's are both recorded, the
hardware one is checked.

[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The runtime loads no quantized packages of the Vela 2.0 family:
it runs at its published precision.
Batches that merge requests run a pre-packed FP32 copy of its linear layers on x86 CPUs with oneDNN, which its records show changes
no decision.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B --engine --platform cpu
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B
        device: auto
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/Vela-2.0-0.3B --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: Vela-2.0-0.3B` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
